svg.text: Hive to Iceberg Lakehouse — Before / After

g.title: Before: Hive tables with no transactions, no rollback, and rewrites on every schema change.
Hive tables with no transactions, so a failed write can leave partial data behind.
A static metastore where schema changes need rewrites, so evolving data is painful.
Changing a schema means rewriting history, which is slow and risky.
No way to read an earlier snapshot, so a bad load cannot be rolled back cleanly.
Backfills run by hand, so they are easy to get wrong and hard to repeat.
No quality gate before a snapshot is promoted, so bad data can become the current version.
Readers and writers share the same state, so queries can see half-written data.

svg.text: How it happens, step by step — follow the numbered nodes in order; each step hands its problems to the next.

g.title: After: Iceberg tables with ACID writes, snapshot time travel, schema evolution, and gated promotion.
Original Hive tables kept as the source, so nothing is lost during migration.
Spark jobs that migrate tables in stages, so each table is proven before it moves.
Iceberg tables on S3 with ACID transactions, so writes are atomic and safe.
Every write creates a snapshot, so any earlier version can be read or rolled back to.
Schema and partition changes apply without rewriting history, so data can evolve safely.
Quality checks run before a snapshot is promoted, so bad data never becomes current.
Airflow orchestrates the migration in stages, so the order and retries are handled for you.
Curated gold aggregates on Iceberg, ready for dashboards and ML features.
